issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): int, but the template explicitly instructs the return type should be double and the solution implements getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() returning double. This inconsistency between the UML and both the template comment and the solution can confuse students about the expected return type and lead to mismatched implementations or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferably update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double to match the template comment and the solution implementation. Alternatively, if an integer result is intended, change the template comment and solution method signature/implementation to return int and update any related documentation accordingly.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() with return type int, while the template's hint and the solution implementation use a double return type for the same method. This mismatch in the method signature across artifacts can confuse students about the expected return type and how to implement/verify the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double (recommended for precision) or change the template hint and solution to use int. Prefer aligning the UML with the template comment and solution (double) so students have a single clear target.
